author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it. All specialties render on one page, reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory at /specialties.html is opened, then every stored specialty is listed by its stored name.
Given a specialty that veterinarians hold, when the directory is opened, then each holder is named first name then last name, such as "Helen Leary".
Given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on the page.
Given every specialty the clinic knows, when the directory is opened, then all of them appear on one page, with no paging.
Given any page of the system, when it is rendered, then it carries no navigation entry or link to the specialty directory.
Edge case 1: a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, shown as held by none rather than left blank.
Edge case 2: a veterinarian holding two specialties is shown under each of them.
Edge case 3: the specialties, and the veterinarians within each, are presented in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one.
non_goals: Any navigation entry or link leading to the page; a visible entry point is a possible follow-up request
Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2 unchanged)
Listing veterinarians who hold no specialty; the page lists specialties, not the roster
Translating a stored specialty name; it is data and appears as stored
notes: Boundary check: read-only view, so NG-2 stands unchanged and the Non-Goals table is untouched (no scope_overrides needed). NG-9 is untouched too: the page takes no query, so it is a listing rather than a search. REQ-SYS-001 still binds, so the new page carries the existing navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory; it just gains no entry pointing back at itself. REQ-LANG-002 binds the page's own wording across all eleven bundles. Two narrowest readings taken where the request was silent, both recorded in the PRD Open Questions: entry order is stable but unspecified (edge case 3, mirroring the veterinarian directory), and a specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed since the page lists every specialty the clinic knows (edge case 1).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice instantiates in-force patterns only: one Repository, one Web controller, one Value object, one Thymeleaf page in the existing vet feature package (system-design.md#package-structure, ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization, ADR 2026-07-31-server-side-rendering-with-thymeleaf). The adjustment is small but real: no repository over Specialty exists today, and the veterinarian collection alone cannot yield a specialty no veterinarian holds. SpecialtyRepository follows the PetTypeRepository precedent (a repository over a lookup value) while keeping VetRepository's narrow Repository base rather than JpaRepository. The specialty-to-veterinarian view is assembled in the application as an immutable read model, SpecialtyDirectory, named for the ubiquitous-language term added 2026-08-30. Grouping and ordering live there rather than in the controller, so the Web controller row of the pattern catalog (holds no business rule) is honored and the projection is unit-testable without MVC. docs/system-design.md gained three Contracts rows and one invariant note; no ADR is warranted, since every choice is local and cheap to reverse.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html is a new route in the vet package; /vets.html and /vets are untouched
SpecialtyController reads VetRepository.findAll() (cached, specialties eager) and SpecialtyRepository.findAll(), then delegates to SpecialtyDirectory
The page reuses fragments/layout with a menu key matching no menuItem, so the standing navigation renders and nothing links to the new page
No new message key is required: #{specialties}, #{name}, #{vets}, #{none} already exist in all eleven bundles

patterns.description: repository over a lookup value; the precedent SpecialtyRepository follows, but keep VetRepository's narrower Repository base and a single findAll()
ordering by NamedEntity name with a Java comparator; SpecialtyDirectory orders specialties the same way
rendering conventions to mirror: 'firstName + " " + lastName' for a veterinarian, #{none} for an empty cell, layout fragment replace at the html element
MockMvc controller-test shape for the vet package; SpecialtyDirectoryTests stays a plain unit test with real Vet and Specialty instances

risks.risk: Adding an inverse @ManyToMany(mappedBy) from Specialty to Vet would make the /vets serialization route recurse Vet -> Specialty -> Vet, and would add a second eager many-to-many fetch.
risks.mitigation: Do not touch the mapping. Specialty stays without an inverse association; the directory is projected in SpecialtyDirectory from the two independent reads.

risks.risk: Caching the specialty read would extend the unresolved vet-cache question (system-design.md#open-questions-from-the-survey, item 5), which has no eviction and no write path.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyRepository is uncached. The vet read stays on the existing 'vets' cache; CacheConfiguration is untouched.

risks.risk: The page is unpaged by requirement, so both collections load whole on every request.
risks.mitigation: Accepted and bounded: the clinic has no write path for veterinarians or specialties (NG-2), and the seeded sets are three specialties and six veterinarians.

risks.risk: A new user-facing string would have to land in all eleven message bundles or I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails the build (REQ-LANG-002).
risks.mitigation: The template reuses existing keys. If a heading key proves unavoidable, add it to every bundle in the same change.

risks.risk: Sorting inside a query would inherit the vendor divergence recorded under Known Defects (PostgreSQL orders and matches case-sensitively).
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory sorts in Java, so the rendered order is identical on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL.

notes: Deviation from the prd-entry file_targets, deliberate and small: the entry named VetController, VetRepository, and VetControllerTests. VetController already serves two vet routes with its own pagination helper, and a Spring Data repository is typed to one aggregate root, so the specialty read cannot hang off VetRepository cleanly. The owner package's one-controller-per-page shape (OwnerController, PetController, VisitController) is the convention followed instead. The acceptance criteria, test names, and non-goals from the prd-entry are unchanged; the six test names split across SpecialtyDirectoryTests (ordering, the specialty held by none, the veterinarian under two specialties, the veterinarian holding none) and SpecialtyControllerTests (route, view, model, and the rendered 'first last' form). Three PRD open questions resolved with the narrowest reading, since no further product answer will arrive. (1) Entry order: specialties by stored name, then holders by last name and first name, with a deterministic tie-break on identity; sorting happens in SpecialtyDirectory. (2) A specialty no veterinarian holds is listed with the existing #{none} wording, mirroring how vetList.html renders a veterinarian with no specialty. (3) The deferred entry point: the page takes the shared layout with a menu value matching no navigation item, so REQ-SYS-001's navigation still renders and no item points at /specialties.html; a later slice adding an entry changes one argument. Security: the route takes no query parameter and no path variable, so it crosses no new trust boundary; stored names are echoed through Thymeleaf's default escaping, which the existing Threat Model row already covers. No authentication exists anywhere (NG-1), so the page is as open as every other route, and it exposes no data the veterinarian directory does not already show. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit had nothing to judge.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectory.of/indexHoldersBySpecialtyId documents and justifies the identity-keyed index (Specialty defines no equality, VetRepository.findAll() is cached) rather than leaving the reader to infer it
Specialty's lack of an inverse association to Vet is explained in both SpecialtyDirectory's class Javadoc and system-design.md, so the omission reads as deliberate rather than missed

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: No NVD match ran in this review: the project configures no OWASP dependency-check plugin (grep of build.gradle for dependencyCheck returns nothing), so ./gradlew dependencyCheckAnalyze does not exist as a task and this reviewer has no network access. The check is therefore not run rather than clean. This is a pre-existing baseline gap, not something this change introduces — the change adds no dependency — so it is recorded here rather than as a finding. A human or CI closing the framework-CVE check for Spring Boot 4.1.0 would be worth scheduling independently of this slice.

Non-blocking, for whoever adds the second uncached read: SpecialtyRepository#findAll is deliberately not @Cacheable (its Javadoc gives the reason — no eviction path). That is the safer choice against a stale directory, and at the current table size the cost is negligible. If the specialties table ever grows, or if a follow-up request links the page into navigation and raises its traffic, revisit the caching decision alongside an eviction path rather than adding @Cacheable("vets") to it, which would share a cache region with a differently-shaped read.
approved_aspects: Output escaping: every value in src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html renders through th:text (entry.specialtyName, veterinarian.firstName/lastName) or a #{...} message key. Thymeleaf's default HTML escaping is on and is not disabled anywhere; no th:utext, no th:href/th:src carrying model data, no inline JavaScript, no remote resource load, no expression-preprocessing (__${...}__) in the new template. A grep sweep of the whole templates/ tree for th:utext and __${ found the pre-existing numeric page-number preprocessing in vetList.html only. Stored specialty and veterinarian names therefore cannot break out as markup — the system-design threat-model row 'Cross-site scripting through rendered user data' holds unchanged.

Pattern consistency: specialtyList.html mirrors vetList.html's escaping and empty-cell (#{none}) construction element for element; the concern is secured the same way as the neighbouring implementation, with no divergence to justify.

Injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository declares one Spring Data derived query (findAll) on the Repository interface with @Transactional(readOnly = true). No JPQL, no native query, no string concatenation, no EntityManager use. Grep of src/main/java for createQuery/createNativeQuery/Runtime./ProcessBuilder returns nothing.

Attack surface: GET /specialties.html takes no @RequestParam, no @PathVariable, and no request body — there is no untrusted input crossing into the handler at all, so the mass-assignment, path-traversal, and cross-request-state rows of docs/security-principles.md are not reachable. The route is read-only and writes nothing. What it exposes (veterinarian names, specialty names) is already published by the pre-existing /vets.html and /vets routes, so the change discloses no new data and does not widen the baseline in docs/system-design.md § Security Context.

Resource use: the unpaged read is not a new resource class. VetController#showResourcesVetList already performs the identical unpaged vetRepository.findAll() on the open /vets route, and that call is @Cacheable("vets"). The one uncached read the change adds is specialtyRepository.findAll() over the specialties lookup table (three seeded rows), joined in memory by SpecialtyDirectory with no nested iteration beyond holders-per-vet. No unbounded allocation attributable to request input, since no request input reaches the query.

Concurrency and state: SpecialtyController is a stateless singleton holding only two repository references; SpecialtyDirectory and its Entry are final, built once per request from defensively re-collected List.of()/toList() lists, and expose no mutator. No shared mutable state, no non-thread-safe formatter.

Secrets: the diff introduces no credential, token, key, connection string, or URL. No logging statements at all are added, so no path exists for stored data or internal detail to reach a log line or an error message.
Supply chain: scripts/changeset.sh --name-only confirms build.gradle is untouched — no new dependency, no repository change, and the mavenCentral() TLS resolution baseline is unaltered.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Every one of the five SpecialtyDirectoryTests cases (and the SpecialtyControllerTests setup) passes the *same* Specialty object instance into both the specialties collection and the holding veterinarian's addSpecialty(...). SpecialtyDirectory.of's own javadoc says matching happens by stored id 'because the two reads that feed it may return separate instances of the same row' -- but no test ever constructs two distinct Specialty instances sharing an id to exercise that exact scenario. As written, the suite would stay green even if indexHoldersBySpecialtyId regressed to keying on object identity (or a HashSet/equals-based join) instead of Specialty.getId(): every specialty would then render as held by none once the vet cache and the specialty read return separate instances, and nothing here would catch it. This is the coverage gap the implementer flagged, confirmed real.
findings.fix: Add a test (e.g. theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldMatchHoldersAcrossSeparateInstancesOfTheSameSpecialty) that builds two separate Specialty objects with the same id and different object identity -- one placed in the specialties list passed to SpecialtyDirectory.of, a distinct instance (same id) attached via addSpecialty to a veterinarian -- and asserts the veterinarian still appears as a holder. Extend the specialtyNamed factory (or add a specialtyWithId(id, name) variant) so the id can be supplied explicitly to construct the second instance.

findings.description: specialtyNamed(...) and veterinarianNamed(...) are byte-for-byte duplicated across the two new test classes, including the private nextStoredId counter. The implementer's justification ('kept local to match VetControllerTests' existing idiom') does not hold: VetControllerTests uses ad hoc per-vet methods (james(), helen()), not this named-factory pattern, so there is no existing idiom being matched -- this is new duplication introduced by the slice itself, in the same package, testing objects from the same production classes.
findings.fix: Extract specialtyNamed, veterinarianNamed, and the id counter into one package-private test-support class (e.g. VetFixtures) in org.springframework.samples.petclinic.vet, and have both SpecialtyDirectoryTests and SpecialtyControllerTests call it instead of each keeping a local copy.

approved_aspects: All three PRD edge cases and all five acceptance criteria have dedicated tests, including the previously-untested AC5 (no self-referencing navigation entry) and edge case 2 (multi-specialty holder), matching the implementer's stated additions
Four-phase structure observed with no phase comments; test names follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD school
Construction goes through factory methods rather than raw constructors, and irrelevant ids are generated via a counter rather than hard-coded, per the three-tier data naming convention
MockMvc is the only mock boundary in SpecialtyControllerTests, consistent with the brief's sanctioned-mock policy; SpecialtyDirectoryTests uses only real Vet/Specialty instances
./gradlew test passes for both new classes

author: change-grader
summary: add specialty directory read model, repository, controller, and page

blast_radius.note: Purely additive within one module: four new files in the existing vet package plus one Thymeleaf page, zero lines deleted from any production source, and no existing controller, entity, repository, layout fragment, or message bundle touched. The only new external surface is GET /specialties.html, which collides with no existing mapping; the three doc files carry the rest of the delta.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunks, the code does what its size and description promise. The specialty-to-holder join keys on Specialty.getId() rather than object identity or equality, which is the correct choice given the vet read is cached and may return detached instances of the same row, and the javadoc says so. Both comparators pin ties with a nullsLast id, the entries and holders lists are toList() immutables, and the template escapes both name fields through th:text. Two behaviors are worth knowing rather than fearing: the two reads run in separate read-only transactions with different cache lifetimes (VetRepository is @Cacheable on the vets cache, SpecialtyRepository deliberately is not), so a concurrent write could in principle produce a torn or stale join; and specialty ordering is case-sensitive String natural order. Both are inert against seeded lowercase data on a read-only demo page, and both were reasoned about in the design record.

test_adequacy.note: The tests exercise the changed behavior rather than restate it. SpecialtyDirectoryTests covers each boundary the code actually decides: a specialty no veterinarian holds, a veterinarian holding none, a veterinarian under two specialties, full ordering, and the cross-instance identity join that would silently empty every holder list under an equality-keyed regression. SpecialtyControllerTests renders the real template through MockMvc and asserts on emitted content, not just on model attributes. A broken implementation fails these. One thin spot: the no-navigation acceptance bullet reads any page of the system and only this page is asserted, though the shared layout fragment renders inside that assertion, so a regression adding a menu entry would still be caught.

reviewer_hedging.note: Three of the four round-2 approvals are silent, but the security reviewer approved with an explicit reservation parked in recommendations: supply chain was not verified this round either, because the project configures no OWASP dependency-check plugin and the reviewer had no NVD access, and the reviewer asks that this be recorded as not verified rather than clean. The delta adds and removes no dependency, so the resolved artifact set is unchanged and the gap is a pre-existing project-level one rather than something this slice introduced. Round 1 also reworked a bar_clause-flagged PRD clause under a critical, blocked finding; that one was accepted, superseded, and re-approved cleanly.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, zero consultations, zero design revisions, and one module touched. The shipped files match the design record's primary_paths exactly, and the only addition, the VetFixtures test helper, arose from a round-1 test-reviewer finding rather than from drift. The two questions the change could not settle on its own, entry ordering and the missing entry point, were pushed to the PRD Open Questions instead of being resolved by fiat in code.

rationale: The code itself reads clean: contained, additive, correctly identity-joined, and genuinely tested at its boundaries. The concern is procedural rather than a suspected defect. The security reviewer approved while asking that the supply chain be recorded as unverified against the NVD, a standing project gap this slice neither caused nor closed. Confirm you accept that gap, then merge.
